description: Bank-side counterpart disclosure — the licensed banks' own investor-relations/press pages and their CRPS (Centralni registar privrednih subjekata) filings, where an approved board member is registered.

CBCG annual reports (Godišnji izvještaj) and Assembly-submitted reports typically contain the organigram, headcount, and a summary of approvals granted during the year — not yet enumerated as collectible artefacts.
No Cyrillic-script queries were executed (e.g. ЦБЦГ, гувернер, вицегувернер, именовање, саопштење).

EU accession-related supervisory reporting (European Commission Montenegro country report, chapters 4/9; ECB and EBA cooperation notes) that comments on CBCG supervisory capacity and reorganisation was not covered in this cell.
Robots.txt, rate limits, and anti-bot posture of cbcg.me, sluzbenilist.me, skupstina.me and zzzcg.me were not assessed.

Of the 11 CBCG-licensed banks, direct career-page URLs were pinned for 7 (CKB via ATS, NLB, Erste, Addiko, Prva, Adriatic, Ziraat). Career channels for Lovćen, Zapad, Universal Capital and Hipotekarna were not located; Hipotekarna and Zapad have confirmed governance pages but no confirmed hiring page.
Leadership/governance pages were pinned for CKB, Hipotekarna, Addiko and Zapad only. No management-body page was located for NLB, Erste, Prva, Lovćen, Universal Capital, Adriatic or Ziraat.

Bank governance pages are current-state rosters with no publication dates, so they reveal that a change happened but not when. Career pages likewise delete expired vacancies, destroying the hiring time series.

Montenegro's official language is written in both Latin and Cyrillic, and 'crnogorski' is distinct from 'srpski' in official usage. All sources found here were Latin-script; no Cyrillic-script variants of bank pages were searched for or found, and the run's language codes list only sr/en.

This cell is scoped to banks' own corporate channels, but two adjacent pointer layers that would materially improve recall were only touched lightly: the Montenegrin employment agency / job-board layer (ZZZCG and commercial portals) that banks post 'konkurs' notices to, and each bank's foreign parent-group newsroom (OTP, NLB Group, Erste Group, Addiko Group, Ziraat, AikGroup), where a Podgorica CEO appointment is often announced at group level first.

Two of the eleven banks route hiring through a third-party ATS (Talentlyft) rather than their own HTML, and CKB's own site exposes both legacy .html and clean-path URLs for the same management content — signs of mid-migration site estates.

No confirmed source found for the Montenegro presence of major international core-banking/payments vendors beyond the Asseco/Payten and Printec families (e.g. Temenos, Oracle FSS, Finastra, BPC, OpenWay, Nets/Nexi, Worldline, Idemia, Thales).
No people-level appointment source is lawfully collectable: no ME equivalent of an executive-appointments wire was identified for the supplier layer.
ICT Cortex full member directory URL, MFIC full member list URL and the Payten Montenegro local page were inferred from search snippets rather than opened; exact directory paths are unconfirmed.
Serbian-language searching used standard ekavian/ijekavian business terms; no Cyrillic-script variants were tried, and Montenegrin-specific orthography (s'/z') was not exercised.

Bank-side procurement/tender visibility for private banks was not tested in this cell (public e-procurement covers state bodies only), and no supplier-side tender-award announcements for ME banks were found.
The canonical UBCG website and its 'Članice' / 'Organi' pages are unresolved.

Committee-level chairs (as opposed to top boards) are only partially visible: the Chamber's banking board president/deputy and MFIC's Banking Committee membership are known, but the named chairs of MFIC's other committees and of any UBCG working groups (digitalisation/AI, ESG, AML/CFT — newly created per the 2026 statute) are not.
Three candidate domains in this slice (ubcg.info, ictcortex.me, and the aktuelno.me tag path) are inferred rather than observed as links in search results.

Bilateral and diaspora chambers other than AmCham (e.g. Italian, Turkish, German-affiliated business councils in Montenegro) were not searched, and neither were the Montenegrin Bar/notary or auditor/accountant professional bodies whose committee seats often overlap with bank compliance and finance leadership.
No archived snapshots of any of these member directories were located, so historical membership/board turnover cannot currently be reconstructed.

Individual bank newsrooms were not systematically enumerated in this cell. Each Montenegrin bank (CKB, NLB Banka, Erste Bank AD Podgorica, Hipotekarna banka, Lovcen banka, Addiko Bank Montenegro, Prva banka, Zapad banka, Universal Capital Bank, Adriatic Bank, Ziraat Bank Montenegro) publishes its own award and conference-participation press releases naming executives with titles.

Conference sites in this market overwrite the current edition and rarely keep speaker archives; INFINTECH keeps a /infintech-2024/ page but MFM Conference did not present an obvious archive of prior editions. Historical title assertions will be lost if not snapshotted at the time.

Much Montenegrin conference and award material — speaker cards, panel photos with name/title captions, ceremony videos — is published only on LinkedIn, Facebook and YouTube rather than on websites. Observed examples: the AMM Facebook page and its YouTube channel, Mastercard Crna Gora Facebook, and bank LinkedIn pages (e.g. Erste banka Crna Gora) that announce awards and appointments.

Coverage in this pass used Montenegrin/Serbian Latin script without diacritics. Montenegrin content also appears in Cyrillic (notably Dan/DAN) and with full diacritics (c, c, s, z, dj), and Montenegrin-specific letters (s, z) are used by some outlets. Query variants for these were not exercised.

Sponsor and exhibitor lists — the strongest signal of which payment vendors are active locally — were only partially captured. Visa was confirmed as MFM Platinum sponsor and Logate as INFINTECH organiser, but full sponsor walls for INFINTECH and MFM were not retrieved, and no vendor-side event (Payten, ASEE, Diebold, NCR, Printec-class suppliers) was identified in Montenegro.

Academic and executive-education programmes in Montenegro (Univerzitet Crne Gore Ekonomski fakultet, Univerzitet Donja Gorica, Mediteran) that run banking/finance postgraduate and executive courses were not searched. Guest-lecturer and programme-council lists at these institutions are a classic dated title registry for bank executives.
No confirmed direct source (site, social account, contact page) for the banking/finance branch trade union(s) of Montenegro, despite them being the signatory of the sector collective agreement.
Službeni list Crne Gore was not directly searched, so the in-force text and amendments of the banking branch collective agreement, and any registered strike/redundancy-related acts, are unconfirmed.
Vijesti.me, Pobjeda.me, Analitika/Aktuelno and Borba.me labour sections were not directly searched; only incidental hits appeared.
No per-bank labour-conflict baseline exists yet (which Montenegrin banks have had strikes, union chapters, mass dismissals or manager-dismissal litigation).
It is unresolved whether AMRRS dispute records, labour-inspectorate findings and ZZZCG collective-dismissal notifications can be obtained at employer granularity.

None of the listed URLs were fetched in this run; all are search-derived and unverified for reachability or current structure (notably amrrs.gov.me, socsav.me and the gov.me PDF endpoints, which have known host/CMS instability).

EIB, the Council of Europe Development Bank, the Western Balkans Investment Framework (WBIF) and the WB6 Chamber were not searched at all; WBIF in particular publishes project pages and technical-assistance ToRs naming Montenegrin financial-sector beneficiaries.

IFI recruitment channels — EBRD/IFC/World Bank consultancy and staff vacancy portals, and WBIF/EU tender notices (TED) for Montenegro financial-sector TA — were not covered, yet they are the most direct 'jobs/hiring' evidence in this cell.
Only one Montenegrin/Serbian-language query was executed; sr-language coverage of IFI and EU material (CBCG saopštenja, Vijesti/Pobjeda/Dan business desks, Analitika) is thin in this slice.

Foreign-press wires (Reuters, Bloomberg, bne IntelliNews, Euromoney, The Banker, Global Finance awards) covering Montenegrin bank ownership and management change were not reached before the search budget ran out.
The IFC disclosure portal and rating-agency sites are JS/registration gated and could not be enumerated with plain fetches.
Croatian- and Bosnian-language regional business press is absent from this slice (Poslovni dnevnik HR, Lider, Jutarnji/Novac, Klix.ba, Capital.ba, Nezavisne novine, Faktor.ba).
Regional news agencies/wires that regional portals republish (Tanjug, Beta, Fonet, Hina, MINA cooperation feeds) were not reached, nor were regional aggregator/press-clipping services.

Professional-network and corporate-comms channels used by regional banking groups (LinkedIn company pages for Agri Europe/AIK, NLB, OTP, Erste, Addiko; group press-release rooms) were not scouted in this cell, although they are the primary origin of subsidiary appointment announcements the regional press then repeats.
Merger-integration effects on staff (redundancies, branch consolidation, role changes) are asserted by analysis pieces but no source was found that reports them concretely for Montenegro.

Several high-value endpoints were identified structurally but not fetched in this pass: otpgroup.info announcement year-indexes, belex.rs AIK issuer disclosure feed, adhoc.pressetext.com archive structure, kap.org.tr issuer search, and the canonical Alta banka domain.

Montenegrin bank ownership is actively changing (AikGroup took 74.9% of Hipotekarna banka in 2025; NLB announced an intention to launch a voluntary takeover offer for Addiko in April 2026). The foreign-parent watchlist for this cell will go stale quickly.

The glossary used was assembled ad hoc during search; systematic Montenegrin governance vocabulary (odbor direktora, izvršni direktor, glavni izvršni direktor, uprava banke, nadzorni odbor, skupština akcionara, imenovanje/razrješenje, sticanje kvalifikovanog učešća) was not yet exhaustively tested against each source.

Several Montenegrin banks have foreign or offshore owners not covered by the named group set: Adriatic Bank (100% Adriatic Capital LLC, Delaware), Universal Capital Bank, Zapad Banka, First Financial Bank. No group-level press or IR channel was identified for these.

For the 'jobs/hiring' half of workstream A5, only NLB and Erste group careers portals were located at parent level; OTP, Addiko and Ziraat group career feeds for Montenegro were not identified, and LinkedIn is ToS-blocked for automation.
Payment-system operators licensed by CBCG are not yet named, because the register page exposes them only via a linked PDF.

Three of the seven licensed payment institutions — CAPITAL TRANSFER MNE DOO, Business Integration and Business Intelligence d.o.o., and (beyond the CompanyWall profile) ALTA PAY GROUP DOO — were not individually profiled for web presence, careers channel or named management in this pass.
The agents of licensed PIs (the retail cash-in/cash-out network) are listed in the CBCG register but were not enumerated, and their hiring is largely invisible outside classifieds.
CBCG 'fit and proper' consents and licensing decisions for PI management were inferred as a route to named appointments but no concrete decision page or bulletin URL was located.

English-language searching added essentially nothing beyond the vendor layer (Payten/Asseco). Montenegrin payments hiring and leadership content is published almost exclusively in Montenegrin/Serbian.

The two richest leadership/headcount sources — CompanyWall ME and LinkedIn — are respectively freemium and scraping-prohibited, so the most granular data on director changes and staff counts is not freely automatable.

Montenegro Transfers presents itself as part of Altapay Group while ALTA PAY GROUP DOO is separately licensed — a probable single ownership cluster holding two register entries. This linkage came from site branding, not from a register, and is unverified.

Coastal hubs (Tivat/Porto Montenegro, Budva, Herceg Novi) where relocated crypto and nomad-founded fintech teams cluster have almost no indexed local-language source coverage; only a single Budva crypto-exchange site was found.
Founder-community channels (Telegram, Discord, Facebook groups such as 'Startup Montenegro', nomad/expat groups) were not explored; they carry hiring and relocation announcements first.
The Montenegrin central company register (CRPS) was not examined in this pass; it would corroborate director changes and new company/branch registrations by fintech entrants.
Local and regional executive-search/staffing agencies placing fintech country managers in ME were not identified.
Little 2025-2026 material surfaced for local startup hiring; unclear which local sources are still actively publishing.

First-party career pages were confirmed for CKB (TalentLyft), Erste, Lovćen, Universal Capital, Prva banka and CBCG, but not yet located for NLB Banka Podgorica, Hipotekarna Banka, Addiko Bank Montenegro, Adriatic Bank, Zapad banka or Ziraat Bank Montenegro.

Coverage is bank-centric. Non-bank payment institutions, e-money institutions, card processors, ATM/POS service companies and IT-in-finance vendors serving Montenegrin banks were not enumerated, so their vacancies are not being captured.
The ZZZCG notice indicates vacancies are legally published in the daily newspaper 'Dan' on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. No digital archive of Dan's vacancy pages was identified in this pass.

Vacancy pages across every board observed expire and are removed (deadline-passed markers on ZZZCG, expiry countdowns on zaposli.me, a lapsed 2025 CKB ad on prekoveze.me). Without snapshotting, the leading-indicator value is lost within weeks.
Albanian-language vacancy channels serving Ulcinj/Tuzi (where CKB has a branch presence) were not searched in this pass, and no Albanian job-board terms were used.

ATS platforms were only confirmed for one bank (CKB/TalentLyft). ATS tenants typically expose stable JSON endpoints that are far more reliable than HTML scraping, and no systematic probe for such endpoints was performed.
The cell's core signal (individual 'new role' posts, People tabs, Alumni tool, job-post history) requires a logged-in LinkedIn session, which this pass did not have.
LinkedIn presences unmapped for Addiko Bank Podgorica, Ziraat Bank Montenegro, Zapad banka, and for non-bank payment institutions licensed by CBCG.
Montenegrin/Serbian role-change phrasing was used in queries but produced few genuine hits externally, so the local-language phrase list is untested against real post volume.
People aggregators (ZoomInfo, SignalHire, EMIS) carry stale and paywalled role data and cannot by themselves date a leadership move.
This cell is entirely personal-data-heavy and governed by platform ToS plus GDPR-equivalent Montenegrin data-protection rules.

Dan (dan.co.me) — a named cell target and one of the two most likely outlets for contested dismissal reporting — could not be reached at all (403 on every path tried). Its section structure, search endpoint and feed availability are entirely unknown.

The local-language glossary used here (kadrovske promjene, smjena, razriješen, imenovan, ostavka, otkazi, zatvaranje filijala/ekspoziture, odbor direktora, nadzorni odbor, glavni izvršni direktor) was assembled from observed article titles, but was never validated against a real corpus of Montenegrin bank personnel articles because search would not surface them. Noisy terms are also unflagged — notably 'Pobjeda' (an outlet name AND the common noun 'victory', which polluted every query) and 'Dan' (an outlet name AND the word 'day').

Trade-union and works-council voice is not covered by any source found in this cell. Layoff and restructuring disputes are usually first articulated by a union (Unija slobodnih sindikata Crne Gore / Savez sindikata Crne Gore and any banking-sector branch), and media only report them once the union speaks. No union source or union-sector-branch page was located during this sweep.

Broadcast-only outlets (TV Vijesti, Nova M / TV Prva, RTCG television) were not assessed. Interviews with newly appointed bankers frequently air on television and are only partially transcribed to the web, meaning appointment context is lost to a text-only pipeline.

No archival/back-catalogue access route was established for any outlet. All the endpoints found expose only current content; feeds are rolling windows. Reconstructing a multi-year history of who led which Montenegrin bank when — the baseline any leadership-move signal is measured against — is not currently possible from these sources.

MINA's full agency wire (MINA-business) is the upstream origin of much downstream bank-appointment coverage, but its subscription terms, price and delivery format (feed vs. email vs. portal) were not established — the business section returned 403 and no pricing page was reached.
Whether CRPS exposes officer/authorised-person data to unauthenticated search, and whether there is a machine-readable endpoint or bulk download, is unresolved.
The lag between an actual board/representative change, its CRPS filing, its gazette publication (where applicable) and its appearance in OpenCorporates/CompanyWall is unknown.

No source found in this cell covering court-register / insolvency and liquidation proceedings (stečaj, likvidacija) for financial entities, which are organization-change events adjacent to the register.
GLEIF/LEI records and MONSTAT's statistical business register were hypothesised as complementary entity-identifier sources but not searched in this run.
Personal-data (GDPR-aligned Montenegrin Zakon o zaštiti podataka o ličnosti) constraints on systematically compiling named directors' histories were not assessed.

Uprava prihoda i carina Crne Gore (revenue and customs, a large payments-adjacent state body) has no confirmed own vacancy/appointment page; only its Facebook/X presence and the central uzk.gov.me register were located.
Kreditno-garantni fond Crne Gore (Credit Guarantee Fund) was only reached through media and Government communiques; its own website/domain was not identified.
Državni trezor / Direktorat za trezor within the Ministry of Finance, and the state Treasury's payment-execution unit, were not reachable as distinct, separately-published sources.
No RSS/API/structured feed was confirmed for any of the core official sources (uzk.gov.me, gov.me kadrovska pitanja, sluzbenilist.me).

Latin-script Montenegrin terms were used throughout; Cyrillic variants (јавни конкурс, именовање, управни одбор) and diacritic-stripped variants (zaposljavanje, imenovanje, uprava za ljudske resurse) were not systematically tested.
Historical/archival coverage is thin: uzk.gov.me notes listings older than 1 Sep 2018 are archived separately, and Službeni list retrieval by issue register was not exercised.
Local/municipal public bodies with treasury or payment functions (Glavni grad Podgorica finance secretariat, municipal Odbor za izbor i imenovanja) were noticed but not scouted.
